{{Short description|Italian mathematician}}
[[Image:Cornalba maurizio.jpg|thumb|Maurizio Cornalba, Berkeley 1975]]
'''Maurizio Cornalba''' (born 17 January 1947) is an Italian mathematician, specializing in [[algebraic geometry]].

Cornalba completed his undergraduate studies at [[University of Pisa]] in 1969 and his graduate studies at the [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa]] in 1970. He was a postdoc at [[Princeton University]] from 1970 to 1971 and an assistant professor at the University of Pisa from 1971 to 1976; he was on leave of absence for the academic year 1971–1972 at Princeton University, for the academic year 1974–1975 at [[Harvard University]], and for the academic year 1975–1976 at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. At the [[University of Pavia]] he was a full professor from 1976 to 2017, when he retired as professor emeritus.<ref name=homepage>{{cite web|title=Maurizio Cornalba|website=Dipartimento di Matematica - Università di Pavia|url=http://mate.unipv.it/cornalba/}}</ref>

Cornalba's research deals with the geometry of [[algebraic curve]]s and the geometry and topology of [[moduli space]]s.

He was in 1993/94, 2005 and 2007 at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], in 1995 at the [[Institut Henri Poincaré]], in 1998 at the [[University of Amsterdam]], and in 1984/85 at [[Brown University]].<ref name=homepage/>

In 1975 he received the [[Bartolozzi Prize]]. He is a member of the [[Accademia dei Lincei]] (elected in 1990 a corresponding member and in 2005 a full member), the [[Istituto Lombardo Accademia di Scienze e Lettere]] (elected in 2000), and the {{ill|Accademia delle Scienze di Torino|it}} (elected in 2011).<ref name=homepage/>

In 1998 he was an Invited Speaker with talk ''Cohomology of Moduli Spaces of Stable Curves'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book|author=Cornalba, Maurizio|chapter=Cohomology of moduli spaces of stable curves|title=''In:'' Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, 1998, Berlin|volume=2|pages=249–257|year=1998|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011660000}} [https://www-dimat.unipv.it/cornalba/slidesICM98.pdf slides for ICM talk]</ref>

He was one of the co-authors for [[Guido Castelnuovo]]'s ''Opere matematiche: memorie e note'', published in 4 volumes by the [[Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei]] from 2002 to 2007, and for [[Phillip Griffiths]]'s ''Selected works'', published in 4 volumes by the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2003.

==Selected publications==
*with [[Enrico Arbarello]], Phillip Griffiths, [[Joe Harris (mathematician)|Joe Harris]] ''Geometry of algebraic curves'', Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften, Springer Verlag, 2 vols., 1985, 2011; [https://books.google.com/books/about/Geometry_of_Algebraic_Curves.html?id=LanxBwAAQBAJ Vol. 1, 2013 pbk reprint]; [https://books.google.com/books?id=suKBB4r5woEC Vol. 2, 2011 pbk edition]
*with E. Arbarello, P. Griffiths, Joe Harris, ''Special divisors on algebraic curves'', reprinted in ''Selected Works of Phillip Griffiths'', vol. 2, American Mathematical Society 2003, pp.&nbsp;649–778 (Lecture notes, Regional Algebraic Geometry Conference, Athens, Georgia, 1979)
*as editor with X. Gomez-Mont, A. Verjovsky [https://books.google.com/books/about/Lectures_On_Riemann_Surfaces_Proceedings.html?id=pWEGCwAAQBAJ ''Lectures on Riemann Surfaces''] (ICTP, Triest 1987), World Scientific 1989
*as editor with Fabrizio Catanese, Ciro Ciliberto ''Problems in the theory of surfaces and their classification'', Symposia Mathematica 32, Academic Press, London, 1991.
